{
  "tag_name": "v1.10.26-qa",
  "name": "IVX Holdings v1.10.26 — the Home black screen was a missing line",
  "draft": false,
  "prerelease": false,
  "body": "## The Home black screen: one missing line

`app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` — the real defect:

```js
const TABS_LOADING_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000;

useEffect(() => {
  if (!isLoading) {
    setLoadingTimedOut(false);
    // setAuthInitError(null)  <-- THIS LINE DID NOT EXIST
    return;
  }
  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    setLoadingTimedOut(true);
    setAuthInitError('IVX startup took too long...');
  }, TABS_LOADING_TIMEOUT_MS);
  return () => clearTimeout(timer);
}, [isLoading]);
```

When auth finished, the code reset `loadingTimedOut` but **never cleared `authInitError`**. And the `if (authInitError)` branch returns **before** `<Tabs>` is ever rendered.

So a single launch slower than 2 seconds — routine on mobile data, where the Supabase session call regularly exceeds two seconds — permanently replaced the entire tab tree, **Home included, for the whole session**. Auth succeeding did not bring Home back. Navigating did not bring Home back. Nothing threw, so no error boundary, no crash log, and no error screen ever reported it.

**Fixed:** the missing `setAuthInitError(null)`, plus the timeout raised 2000ms -> 12000ms because 2 seconds was never a realistic budget for a real device on a real network.

## One of the black screens was my own diagnostic

`BlankScreenWatchdog` mounted a full-screen **opaque** layer directly above the entire app:

```js
overlay: {
  ...StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject,
  backgroundColor: '#0A0A0F',
  zIndex: 9999,
}
```

`#0A0A0F` is `rgb(10,10,15)`. The device recording measured `rgb(12,8,14)`.

It never caught a single real defect. It falsely accused working screens twice, and its own recovery button navigated into a route that rendered nothing. A diagnostic that can paint the whole screen near-black is not a safety net — it is another way to get a black screen. **Deleted.**

## Why this kept coming back

Four different waiting states all used the identical near-black `#0A0A0F`: root startup, routing, sign-in, and that overlay. A screenshot of a stuck app could not distinguish them, so every diagnosis was a guess.

Each stage now owns a distinct colour and prints its own name:

- **STAGE 1 - STARTING** — `#0A0A0F` (root startup)
- **STAGE 2 · ROUTING** — `#0B1220` navy (route `/`)
- **STAGE 3 · SIGNING IN** — `#141007` warm dark (tabs auth)

One screenshot now names the exact stage.

## Validation

- `runChecks` (TypeScript + lint + structure): **0 errors**
- Routing + crash-shield suites: **46 pass / 0 fail**
- Full suite: **1192 pass**, 3 pre-existing unrelated failures (unchanged)
- Gradle: **BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 38s**

### Verified inside the shipped bundle

The overlay strings are **absent**, confirming the removal:

```
Screen failed to load    ascii=-1 utf16=-1  -> GONE
Go to Home               ascii=-1 utf16=-1  -> GONE
Back to Login            ascii=-1 utf16=-1  -> GONE
blank-screen-watchdog    ascii=-1 utf16=-1  -> GONE
```

The new stage labels are **present** (the `·` ones live in Hermes' UTF-16 string table, so an ASCII grep alone would wrongly report them missing):

```
STAGE 1 - STARTING       ascii   offset=1791555
STAGE 2 · ROUTING        utf16   offset=3392230
STAGE 3 · SIGNING IN     utf16   offset=3424632
```

Stamp `1.10.26 (124)`; `(tabs)/(home)` still absent; `IVX Runtime Error`, `Previous Crash Detected`, `IVX Render Error`, `invalid_credentials`, `IVX startup timed out`, `index-route` all retained.

versionName 1.10.26 / versionCode 124
SHA256: `f64e5774935deca02f66d26b8e84ab6c82237f1ba1b53b7b879615f9ac8d13c1`"
}

responseMessageContents.title: Fixed persistent black screen issue on app home after multiple attempts
responseMessageContents.description: After several tries, the black screen problem that users experienced after logging in was finally resolved. The fix addressed a missing error reset that caused the app to stay stuck on a blank screen, and also removed a watchdog overlay that was incorrectly covering the working screen. A new version of the app (1.10.26) was built and shared, with added stage labels to make any future issues easier to identify.
